discussionLead: We gathered a crew half the size of Shackleton’s for a spirited discussion of Endurance, with broad agreement that dog steak sounded pretty good after a steady diet of penguin and seal hoosh. Lots of new faces tonight — your contributions were much appreciated. A reminder that the December meeting (12/17) will be at my house; I’ll include details in the next poll email. For those travelling over the holidays, be safe, and don’t delay the start of Inventing the Renaissance.
headline: Rubicon takes February.
deck: A dead heat at the top, three ties in all, and every one of them settled by a single voter.
intro: Nine of you ranked fourteen candidates this round. Rubicon (Holland) finished level with An Immense World on 89 points and took it on the head-to-head, in its first appearance on a ballot, and reads February.
outcome: Winner: Rubicon (89, on tiebreak)   ·   Runner-up: An Immense World (89)   ·   Relegated: The Eureka Machine, Born to Run, The River of Doubt, Easy Money
tieIntro: Three pairs finished level: Rubicon and An Immense World on 89, The Black Count and The Man in the High Castle on 69, and Mayflower and Say Nothing on 68. The methodology calls for a Condorcet head-to-head first: ignore the rest of the ballot and ask how each voter ranked the two against one another.
tieVerdict: All three pairs separated, and all three by the same 5–4 margin. Rubicon beat An Immense World and takes the book. The Black Count beat The Man in the High Castle for sixth, and Mayflower beat Say Nothing for eighth. No fall-through to first-place votes was needed.
notes: A debut winner. Rubicon had never been polled before and went straight to the top, with three first-place votes — the most of any book.
The new arrivals did well. Five books were on the ballot for the first time; Rubicon won and Undaunted Courage finished third on 75.
The River of Doubt is relegated after twenty-four polls, finishing thirteenth on 52 despite a first-place vote.
